summary:
Alagoas recorded 2 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 on a population of ~3.3 million, a rate of about 0.61 per million per year - above the national average. The state sits inside the Northeast concentration the dossiers track: Northeastern states absorbed roughly 38 of the 80 national killings in 2025, and Alagoas itself recorded 6 in 2024, one of the worst state counts that year, so its absolute number swung sharply between dossiers. A single additional case would move the rate dramatically at this population.

No unit-specific legal restriction or enforcement finding was identified; the profile rests on the per-capita count, the above-national 2024 toll and the regional concentration. Paraíba, a neighbouring Northeastern state of similar size, recorded 4 killings in 2025.

sources.summary: ANTRA's 9th annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by SBT News): Brazil recorded 80 murders of trans and travesti people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; per-state 2025 counts - Ceara and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7 each, Goias, Maranhao and Para 5 each, Alagoas 2, Mato Grosso 3; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, over half aged 18-29, 70% Black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; Brazil has led the global ranking since 2008. Gives Alagoas' 2025 count (2) within the per-state ranking.

ANTRA dossier coverage (27 Jan 2025): Brazil led global trans-murder tallies for the 16th consecutive year with 122 killings in 2024, a 16% fall on 2023; victim profile predominantly young, Black, poor and Northeastern, with the population's life expectancy cited at about 35 years; most murders happen in public places, at night, with extreme cruelty; authorities rarely register victims' gender identity, degrading official data; state-by-state 2024 table includes Maranhao and Para with 5 killings each, Alagoas 6, Mato Grosso 8, Goias 2; Antra's president demands effective public policies and honest statistics. Shows Alagoas recorded 6 killings in 2024, among the worst state totals that year.
